subject: Questions on Renewal Rate Card & Mid-term Capacity Exchange
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@brightlabs.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal questions — rate card and potential mid-term top-up

Hi Alex,

Quick question as we prep for our Q3 budget review: our usage for the last two months spiked ~2.5x vs forecast (see attached usage_snapshot_May.csv). We are approaching the end of year renewal and would like clarity on three things before we present to procurement: 

1) If we do a mid-contract top-up of committed units, can we exchange existing committed units across clusters (e.g., shift 20% from non-prod to prod) without penalty?
2) Do uplifts to committed units get the same unit price as at renewal or are they priced at the prevailing rate card (we're looking at BrightLabs_RateCard_v3.pdf you sent)?
3) If we annualize the top-up at renewal, is there an early-renewal incentive (credit or a blended discount) you can offer?

We have one procurement lead (Marco Ruiz) who will also join the thread if we need contract language. Can you send a short set of options — prefer a 1-page summary + a recommended path.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Chen
Head of ML Platforms | BrightLabs
Attachment: usage_snapshot_May.csv
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@brightlabs.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-14T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — rate card and potential mid-term top-up

Hi Sophie — thanks for the snapshot and the clear asks. High-level answers below; I can put these into a 1‑pager and drop a SOW draft if that helps.

Summary (short):
- Exchange across clusters: yes, we support internal reallocation of committed units within an account. No contractual penalty — we track and reconcile at invoice cycle, but we do ask that total committed units remain the same unless you explicitly request an uplift.
- Pricing on mid-contract uplifts: uplifts added mid-contract are priced at the current rate card. If you annualize (roll the uplift into the next renewal), we can apply a blended incentive — see options below.
- Early-renewal incentive: we typically offer staged credits or a blended discount when customers commit to annualizing earlier than planned.

Recommended immediate path (what I’d do if I were in your shoes):
1) Short-term top-up to cover the spike (add 30% committed units for remainder of term) at current rate card.
2) Start an early-renewal conversation now to annualize the top-up at renewal; target: blended 8% discount on the uplifted units (applies only if you commit to 12-months at renewal).
3) We’ll create a simple amendment (SOW_draft_20270621.docx) to capture the top-up and the intent to annualize. Procurement can sign the amendment to enable immediate capacity.

I’ll loop in Sales Ops (Ben) to validate the discount math and legal/proc (Priyom) for amendment language. If this sounds okay I’ll prepare the 1‑pager + SOW and propose a 30-minute call with Marco to lock terms.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_draft_20270621.docx
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal questions — rate card and potential mid-term top-up

Ben / Priyom — forwarding BrightLabs ask. Key points: usage spike, want to shift non-prod->prod, looking for an uplift/annualize path with a small incentive. Deal: DL-4739 (Hub link below).

Options I think we can offer (want your signal on feasibility + numbers):

Option A — Immediate top-up, no annualization incentive
- Add 30% committed units for remainder of term, priced at current rate card (no discount).
- Amendment: effective immediately, billed pro-rata for remaining months.

Option B — Immediate top-up + early-annua lize incentive (recommended)
- Add 30% now at current rate card.
- If BrightLabs signs to annualize that uplift at renewal (commit for next 12 months), apply a blended 8% discount on the uplifted portion effective at renewal.
- Provide a one-time onboarding credit of 5% of uplift cost to offset migration/ops effort.

Option C — Temporary burst + convert later
- Provide surge capacity as a burst (no increase to committed units), charged at on-demand rate for the surge period.
- If they convert to committed within 60 days, convert surge usage to committed at a 5% uplift discount relative to on-demand.

Questions: what does Finance need to approve for Option B? Can we formalize the 8% blended incentive plus 5% onboarding credit? Also confirm we allow cluster exchanges as described (no penalty).

HubSpot: https://hub.redwood.com/deals/DL-4739

Thanks — Alex
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-18T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal questions — rate card and potential mid-term top-up

Alex / Lauren — from a pricing/finance perspective Option B is acceptable if we gate approvals as follows: 

- Blended discount: cap at 8% for uplifted units only and only if customer signs a 12-month renewal that includes the uplifted volume. Finance will require a minimal ARR floor (for this deal DL-4739 that’s $150k ARR) to approve.
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time credit up to 5% of uplifted committed spend, but it must be applied as an invoice credit and cannot be combined with other promotional credits.
- Pro-rated billing: we will bill the top-up pro-rata for the remainder of the term; the annualization triggers the blended discount at renewal invoice cycle.
- Cluster exchange: confirm — allowed as long as total committed units per account are unchanged; we capture movement in the monthly usage report.

I ran rough math on the expected uplift (30% for remainder of term -> ~$21k incremental billing this term). If they annualize at renewal, the blended 8% discount reduces uplifted unit price which amounts to ~ $9k benefit over the year (net of onboarding credit).

If Alex wants to present Option B, I recommend including the ARR floor and an approval flow: Sales -> Finance -> RevOps sign-off. I’ll pre-clear finance for DL-4739 subject to the ARR floor.

-Ben
Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@datapulse.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@brightlabs.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — rate card and potential mid-term top-up

Alex / Sophie — thanks for the clear options. Procurement (me) reviewed internally and BrightLabs is comfortable moving forward with Option B as long as: 

- You provide the short amendment capturing the 30% top-up (pro-rated) and the conditional language for the blended 8% discount to apply at renewal if we annualize.
- The onboarding credit is listed and capped at 5% applied as an invoice credit.
- The ARR floor is documented; BrightLabs confirms estimated ARR will meet your threshold.

Sophie / I would like the amendment and a one-page executive summary to circulate to our CFO by EOD Thursday. Can you send a DocuSign/trackable link once the amendment is ready? We can sign the amendment quickly if language matches.

Thanks — Marco
